parsedVerdict.reasoning:
This unit passes. All three files are infrastructure adapters for one concern: running the Task API. Each file has a clear role:
- http-server.ts is the Express HTTP adapter. It turns request bodies into application inputs (CreateTaskInput, TaskFilter) and turns DomainError into HTTP status codes.
- in-memory-task-repository.ts is the storage adapter. It implements the domain TaskRepository interface.
- server.ts is the process entry point. It only reads the port and calls createApp().listen.

The files use the module's own abstractions consistently. http-server.ts reaches data only through TaskService and never touches the repository's Maps directly. The repository is used only as the default TaskRepository passed to TaskService. Each rule lives in one place inside the module:
- Request parsing is in bodyOf and stringField.
- The error-code-to-HTTP-status mapping is in statusCode.
- Filter matching is only in tasksForProject.

Two small issues are not enough to fail the unit:
- server.ts repeats the port fallback expression (`Number.isFinite(port) ? port : 3000`) twice in the same file.
- createApp's default parameter decides which repository to use, which is wiring work placed inside the HTTP adapter.

I can't see the domain file, so I can't confirm whether the filter logic in tasksForProject repeats a rule that the domain already defines.
